title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 1-2
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 1 to 2 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कारो भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 1 to 2 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 1 to 2.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 1 to 2** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कारो भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कारो भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः । भूतकृद्भूतभृद्भावो भूतात्मा भूतभावनः ॥** **पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः । अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञोऽक्षर एव च ॥**

Vishnu is this very universe, present in everything. The Lord of what was, what is and what will be is that God of gods. He creates every being, protects it, and shines within each one as their own Self. He is the pure Self and the Supreme Self. For the liberated, that God of gods is the final goal. He never perishes, he is the witness who sees all, and he knows the body.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 1 to 2 mean?
faq.a: Vishnu is this very universe, present in everything. The Lord of what was, what is and what will be is that God of gods. He creates every being, protects it, and shines within each one as their own Self. He is the pure Self and the Supreme Self. For the liberated, that God of gods is the final goal. He never perishes, he is the witness who sees all, and he knows the body.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
